nativeFailure.diagnostic: ExpoWidgets was built with C++ interoperability enabled, but HanlinScriptingWidgets current compilation does not enable it.

changes: Source HanlinWidgetSDK assigns the original ExpoWidgets Cxx + Clang import settings to HanlinScriptingWidgets and its public HanlinWidgetUI re-export. Both consumers retain package Swift6.
Existing generate_manifest.py already preserves these settings; evaluated generation updates only the two unified target definitions and the source manifest digest receipt.

update_project.py reads ExpoWidgets' evaluated import flags, maps repository paths to SRCROOT and configures the original Xcode widget host; the existing MiniApps extension cloning path inherits that same configuration.
Only four Xcode Debug/Release configuration objects change, each only OTHER_SWIFT_FLAGS and SWIFT_OBJC_INTEROP_MODE. Target, source, resources, module identities, signing and selectors are unchanged.

closure.scope: Existing direct ExpoWidgets imports and HanlinWidgetUI re-export; no new runtime or dependency.

checks.meaning: Both SPM consumers lack the mode/import settings; all four native host build configurations lack the mode.

checks.scope: Actual SwiftPM source/unified manifests, original setting parity, actual generated target bodies, real Xcode project producer/clone and idempotence.
Regenerate unified package from source manifests.
Regenerate actual project with existing producer.

limitations: No Apple-framework typecheck, simulator run, native tests, CI, artifact download, package installation or full source SDK audit in this lane.
Original producer flags/defines/search paths stay intact; this patch does not claim external cancellation or app behavior is fixed.
